resources.string: Placental disc in section, with the fetal side above and the uterine wall below
Two umbilical arteries carry fetal blood to the placenta. One umbilical vein carries it back to the fetus.
The fetal face of the placental disc. Fetal vessels spread out here before branching into the villi.
A fine tip of the branching villous tree. It holds fetal capillaries and is covered by a thin outer layer, the syncytiotrophoblast.
Maternal blood flows around the villi in this space. Fetal blood stays within the villous vessels during normal exchange.
This maternal vessel passes through the uterine side of the placenta and opens into the intervillous space.
